latin_text: An angel, from what we have said, has perfectly realized his own nature and intellectual qualities. Nevertheless, he does not have a way to fulfill his functions of understanding and contemplation unless he is first surrounded by God with intelligible forms. For this reason the darkness has hitherto been upon the face of the deep. The deep is his intellectual capacity, penetrating and searching everything profound.
english_translation: An angel, from what we have said, has perfectly realized his own nature and intellectual qualities. Nevertheless, he does not have a way to fulfill his functions of understanding and contemplation unless he is first surrounded by God with intelligible forms. For this reason the darkness has hitherto been upon the face of the deep. The deep is his intellectual capacity, penetrating and searching everything profound.
exegesis:
[VERIFIED] Pico's allegorical reading: the darkness on the deep represents the angelic intellect awaiting divine illumination. The "deep" (*abyssus*) is the angel's intellectual capacity—profound, penetrating, searching all things. Yet this capacity remains unfulfilled until God surrounds the angel with intelligible forms. [INFERRED] This clarifies angelic participation: angels are not self-subsistent intellects but receive their intellectual actuality from God. Their knowledge is eternally dependent on divine illumination, yet this dependence is the very structure of their beatitude.

The philosophical function is to establish participated intellection as the foundation of angelic being. Angels exemplify how creatures achieve their perfection through receptivity to divine forms. [VERIFIED] This grounds human mysticism: ascending means aligning one's intellect with angelic intellection, which means receiving divine illumination.

[VERIFIED] Commento Book I (C.1.6) develops pre-incarnate angelic intellection. Oration (O.1.3-O.1.4) describes intellectual ascent. Being & Unity grounds it: participated intellect at the highest creaturely level.
